warriorsPage.title: Restoring Hope,
warriorsPage.subtitle: Behind every diagnosis, there is a human spirit refusing to break. Witness the power of your kindness in the lives of these brave warriors.

anetra.name: Anetra
anetra.shortDesc: Diagnosed with Stage 3C Triple-Negative Breast Cancer while battling heart issues.
anetra.fullStory:
Already a long-term cardiac patient, she was admitted to the hospital in January 2022 for what appeared to be a heart attack. A CT scan revealed three masses, leading to a diagnosis of Stage 3C Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC). Despite managing ongoing health challenges, she has dedicated her three years of remission to advocacy. Known as the 'Big Momma' of her family, she balances caregiving for her children and grandchildren with her own intensive physical therapy.

THE IMPACT: The grant provides a necessary physical and mental 'reset.' For a caregiver and advocate who is constantly pouring into others, this staycation offers the rest required to lower her stress levels and refresh her spirit.

janelle.name: Janelle
janelle.shortDesc: Living with cancer for 16 years, recently confirming spread to her brain.
janelle.fullStory:
Diagnosed with Stage 2B breast cancer in 2010 at age 24, Janelle has lived with cancer for nearly 16 years. In 2012, her cancer became metastatic. Following a period of stability during which she and her husband welcomed twin boys via surrogate, she recently experienced a seizure confirming the cancer has spread to her brain.

THE IMPACT: The grant will support Janelle’s transition into advocacy. She aims to connect with the Metastatic Breast Cancer (MBC) community at the summit to begin sharing her journey and providing hope to others facing similar diagnoses.

jeanelle.name: Jeanelle
jeanelle.shortDesc: Misdiagnosed for being 'too young', she battled Stage 3 TNBC. Now a yoga instructor.
jeanelle.fullStory:
After nearly two years of being misdiagnosed because she was considered 'too young', Jeanelle was diagnosed at age 33 with Stage 3, Grade 3 Triple-Negative Breast Cancer. She endured 23 rounds of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, followed by a double mastectomy. Now serving her community as a patient advocate and yoga instructor.

THE IMPACT: The grant provides tangible tools (yoga mats, blocks) to offer free, trauma-informed wellness programs in Newark. It allows her to provide a safe space for women to manage neuropathy, chronic pain, and mental health challenges.

susan.name: Susan Jean
susan.shortDesc: Professional artist who refused to let a diagnosis dim her creativity.
susan.fullStory:
A professional artist who refused to let a diagnosis dim her creativity. Diagnosed in her late 30s as a mother of a 4th grader, she faced the sudden 'curveball' of cancer at the tail end of a pandemic. Today, while she is grateful to have clear scans, she continues to manage the long-term side effects of a 10-year daily treatment plan.

THE IMPACT: With her grant, Susan hosts Art Journal Circles, gifting supplies to local communities in Las Vegas. She has made it through the metaphorical fire and is now dedicated to bringing 'buckets of water' to those still in the thick of it.

taya.name: Taya
taya.shortDesc: Diagnosed at 26, only ten days before her birthday. Now in remission.
taya.fullStory:
Diagnosed at just 26 years old, Taya’s life was suddenly redefined by Stage 2A Invasive Ductal Carcinoma. While pursuing her degree and working full-time, she underwent an aggressive treatment plan. The journey grew even more challenging when post-surgery pathology shifted her diagnosis to Stage 3. In October 2025, she officially entered remission.

THE IMPACT: During treatment, Taya was too ill to celebrate her son’s birthday. Now in recovery, her dream is to reclaim that lost time by taking her son to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. This grant allows Taya to focus entirely on her son and create a lasting, happy memory with her 'living angel'.

anonymous.name: D.
anonymous.shortDesc: Carries a heavy family history of the disease. Currently unable to work due to treatment.
anonymous.fullStory:
Diagnosed with Stage 2B breast cancer, she carries a heavy family history of the disease, having lost her mother to it. Her treatment journey has been marked by severe chemotherapy-induced fatigue, which has prevented her from working and caused significant financial strain. Her primary focus remains on her recovery and being present for her daughter.

THE IMPACT: The grant provides immediate relief from the stress of meeting basic needs (food and bills). By easing the financial burden until she can safely return to work, this support allows her to focus entirely on completing her treatment and regaining her health.

jocelyn.name: Jocelyn
jocelyn.shortDesc: Single mother navigating a five-year course of treatment while managing financial aftermath.
jocelyn.fullStory:
After a lump appeared in 2020 during the pandemic lockdowns, delayed medical access resulted in the cancer growing significantly and spreading to her underarm and shoulder blade. She underwent aggressive treatment involving three types of chemotherapy, a double mastectomy, the removal of all right-side lymph nodes, radiation, and an oophorectomy. As a single mother without a support system, she is currently navigating a five-year course of chemotherapy medication while managing the long-term physical and financial aftermath of the disease.

THE IMPACT: The grant provides an essential lifeline by preventing recurring utility shut-offs. By securing her home’s electricity, the funding reduces the constant stress of basic survival, allowing her to focus on her health and her child.

monica.name: Monica
monica.shortDesc: Diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2022, she aims to turn her healing into a community resource.
monica.fullStory:
Diagnosed with ovarian cancer in September 2022 following surgery, she completed five rounds of chemotherapy between November 2022 and March 2023. This journey shifted her perspective, teaching her to prioritize her own well-being and to live with deep gratitude for her children and each new day.

THE IMPACT: The dream is to purchase supplies to host handmade craft workshops for others navigating an oncological diagnosis. The grant empowers her to turn her personal healing into a community resource, providing a creative outlet for fellow warriors and fostering connection.

wren.name: Wren
wren.dream: Attend the Living Beyond Breast Cancer Conference
wren.shortDesc: Diagnosed in 2019 with stage 4 triple negative breast cancer.
wren.fullStory: Wren was diagnosed in 2019 with stage 4 triple negative breast cancer. Through our Dream Support Program, she chose to attend the Living Beyond Breast Cancer Conference in Philadelphia, a space for learning, connection, and support among others living with metastatic cancer.

penny.name: Penny
penny.shortDesc: Navigating reconstructive surgeries and caring for her mother, she dreams of celebrating in NYC.
penny.fullStory:
Diagnosed at 49, Penny’s battle has been grueling: three types of chemotherapy, immunotherapy, a mastectomy, and radiotherapy. The journey cost her her hair, a breast for two years, and her sense of physical peace. Despite suffering from anxiety, insomnia, and the weight of being a caregiver for her mother with dementia, Penny remains anchored by her daughter and her new 7-month-old granddaughter. She is currently on a 10-year medication plan.

THE IMPACT: Penny’s 50th birthday dream was a trip to New York, halted by radiotherapy. The €500 grant serves as a foundational contribution toward her flights and accommodation. This is the fulfillment of a life-long wish and a celebration of survival after years of putting her own needs second.

breast.title: Breast Cancer
breast.shortDescription: Breast cancer starts when healthy cells in the breast change and grow out of control.
breast.overviewText: Breast cancer is a disease in which breast cells multiply uncontrollably. It is the most common cancer in women worldwide. Early detection through regular mammograms significantly increases the chances of successful treatment.

symptoms.symptom1: A new lump in the breast or underarm.
symptoms.symptom2: Thickening or swelling of part of the breast.
symptoms.symptom3: Irritation or dimpling of breast skin.
symptoms.symptom4: Redness or flaky skin in the nipple area.
symptoms.symptom5: Pulling in of the nipple or pain in the nipple area.
symptoms.symptom6: Any change in the size or the shape of the breast.

breast.treatmentsIntro: Breast cancer treatment is highly personalized and depends on the stage, location, and biological characteristics of the tumor.

treatment1.title: Surgery
treatment1.desc: Can be breast-conserving (lumpectomy) or mastectomy, depending on tumor extent.

treatment2.title: Systemic Therapies
treatment2.desc: Includes chemotherapy, hormone therapy, and biologically targeted therapies.

breast.appointmentText: We have prepared a list of essential questions to ask your oncologist.

lung.title: Lung Cancer
lung.shortDescription: Cancer that begins in the lungs. It is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide.
lung.overviewText: It forms in the tissues of the lungs, usually in the cells lining the air passages. The two main types are small cell lung cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. Smoking is the main risk factor.

symptoms.symptom1: A persistent cough that doesn't go away or gets worse.
symptoms.symptom2: Coughing up blood or rust-colored sputum.
symptoms.symptom3: Chest pain that worsens with deep breathing or coughing.
symptoms.symptom5: Unexplained weight loss and loss of appetite.

lung.treatmentsIntro: Options vary dramatically based on cell type, cancer stage, and overall patient health.

treatment1.title: Targeted Therapy & Immunotherapy
treatment1.desc: Modern treatments that attack specific abnormalities or boost the immune system.

treatment2.title: Surgery & Radiation
treatment2.desc: To remove the tumor (if localized) or shrink it with high-powered energy beams.

colorectal.title: Colorectal Cancer
colorectal.shortDescription: Cancer affecting the colon or rectum, often starting as polyps.
colorectal.overviewText: Most colorectal cancers start as a growth on the inner lining of the colon or rectum called a polyp. Over time, some polyps can turn into cancer. Regular screening tests are vital for prevention.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent change in bowel habits (diarrhea or constipation).
symptoms.symptom2: Rectal bleeding or blood in your stool.
symptoms.symptom3: Persistent abdominal discomfort (cramps, gas, or pain).
symptoms.symptom4: A feeling that your bowel doesn't empty completely.

colorectal.treatmentsIntro: Treatment depends largely on the stage of cancer, though surgery is common for localized tumors.

treatment1.title: Surgery (Colectomy)
treatment1.desc: Removal of the affected part of the colon and nearby lymph nodes.

treatment2.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Often used after surgery to kill any remaining cancer cells.

colorectal.appointmentText: Talk to your doctor about when to start testing.

prostate.title: Prostate Cancer
prostate.shortDescription: Cancer that forms in the prostate gland in men.
prostate.overviewText: It is one of the most common types of cancer in men. It usually grows slowly and is confined to the prostate gland, where it may not cause serious harm. However, some types are aggressive and can spread quickly.

symptoms.symptom1: Trouble urinating or weak urine flow.
symptoms.symptom2: Need to urinate often, especially at night.
symptoms.symptom3: Blood in the urine or semen.
symptoms.symptom5: Pain in the hips, back, or chest (if spread).
symptoms.symptom6: Weakness or numbness in the legs.

prostate.treatmentsIntro: Treatment ranges from active surveillance (for low-risk cancers) to more aggressive interventions.

treatment1.title: Active Surveillance
treatment1.desc: Closely monitoring the cancer without immediate treatment if it grows very slowly.

treatment2.title: Surgery & Radiation
treatment2.desc: Radical prostatectomy (removing the gland) or using radiation beams.

prostate.appointmentText: Discuss PSA benefits and risks with your urologist.

skin.title: Skin Cancer (Melanoma)
skin.shortDescription: The most serious type of skin cancer, developing in the cells that produce melanin.
skin.overviewText: Melanoma originates in melanocytes (pigment cells). It is less common than other skin cancers but more dangerous because it's more likely to spread (metastasize) if not treated early. UV exposure is the main cause.

symptoms.symptom1: A: Asymmetry (one half of the mole doesn't match the other).
symptoms.symptom2: B: Border irregularity, uneven or blurred edges.
symptoms.symptom3: C: Color varied (shades of brown, black, sometimes red or blue).
symptoms.symptom4: D: Diameter larger than 6mm (pencil eraser size).
symptoms.symptom5: E: Evolving (change in size, shape, or color over time).
symptoms.symptom6: Any sore that doesn't heal or mole that itches/bleeds.

skin.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is the main treatment for early-stage melanomas. Advanced cases require systemic therapies.

treatment1.title: Surgical Excision
treatment1.desc: Removing the melanoma and a margin of healthy skin around it.

treatment2.title: Immunotherapy & Targeted Therapy
treatment2.desc: Drugs that boost the immune system or target specific genetic mutations.

skin.appointmentText: Don't wait. See a dermatologist immediately.

bladder.title: Bladder Cancer
bladder.shortDescription: Cancer beginning in the cells lining the bladder.
bladder.overviewText: Most bladder cancers are urothelial carcinomas. It's often diagnosed early when highly treatable, but has a high recurrence rate, so follow-up is crucial. Smoking is a major risk factor.

symptoms.symptom1: Blood in urine (hematuria), visible or microscopic.
symptoms.symptom2: Frequent or urgent urination.
symptoms.symptom3: Pain or burning sensation when urinating.
symptoms.symptom4: Lower back pain or pain on one side.
symptoms.symptom5: Inability to urinate despite having the urge.
symptoms.symptom6: Weight loss and fatigue in advanced stages.

bladder.treatmentsIntro: Treatment depends on whether the cancer has invaded the bladder muscle wall.

treatment1.title: Transurethral Resection (TURBT)
treatment1.desc: Surgery through the urethra to remove superficial tumors.

treatment2.title: Cystectomy & Intravesical Therapy
treatment2.desc: Bladder removal or using BCG directly into the bladder.

stat1.label: More common in men than women

lymphoma.title: Lymphoma
lymphoma.overviewText: Affects lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell). There are two main types: Hodgkin Lymphoma and Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (more common). It can develop in the lymph nodes, spleen, thymus, or bone marrow.

symptoms.symptom1: Painless swelling of lymph nodes (neck, armpits, or groin).
symptoms.symptom2: Persistent fatigue and lack of energy.

lymphoma.treatmentsIntro: Treatment is highly specific based on the exact lymphoma subtype and its aggressiveness.

treatment1.title: Chemotherapy & Targeted Therapy
treatment1.desc: Using drugs to kill cancer cells or block their growth.

treatment2.title: Stem Cell Transplant
treatment2.desc: To replace diseased bone marrow with healthy cells.

lymphoma.appointmentText: Key questions for your blood specialist.

kidney.title: Kidney Cancer
kidney.shortDescription: Cancer that originates in the kidneys. The most common type is renal cell carcinoma.
kidney.overviewText: Kidneys are blood-filtering organs. Kidney cancer is often detected incidentally during imaging tests for other reasons, as early symptoms can be subtle.

symptoms.symptom1: Blood in the urine (may look pink, red, or cola-colored).
symptoms.symptom2: Persistent pain in the back or side, below the ribs.
symptoms.symptom3: A palpable mass or lump in the abdomen or flank.
symptoms.symptom6: Intermittent fever not caused by infection.

kidney.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is the main treatment for most kidney cancers.

treatment1.title: Nephrectomy (Partial or Radical)
treatment1.desc: Removal of the tumor or the entire affected kidney.

treatment2.title: Targeted Therapy & Immunotherapy
treatment2.desc: Frequently used for advanced or metastatic kidney cancer.

uterine.title: Uterine Cancer (Endometrial)
uterine.shortDescription: Cancer that starts in the lining of the uterus (endometrium).
uterine.overviewText: It is the most common type of uterine cancer. It is often detected at an early stage because it causes abnormal vaginal bleeding, which prompts women to see a doctor.

symptoms.symptom1: Vaginal bleeding after menopause (key symptom).
symptoms.symptom2: Bleeding between menstrual periods.
symptoms.symptom3: Abnormal or watery vaginal discharge, sometimes foul-smelling.
symptoms.symptom6: Unintended weight loss in advanced stages.

uterine.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is the standard and often curative treatment in early stages.

treatment1.title: Hysterectomy
treatment1.desc: Surgery to remove the uterus, often along with tubes and ovaries.

treatment2.title: Pelvic Radiation Therapy
treatment2.desc: Use of external or internal radiation (brachytherapy) to kill remaining cells.

uterine.appointmentText: Crucial questions about your reproductive health.

liver.title: Liver Cancer
liver.shortDescription: Primary cancer starting in liver cells. The most common is hepatocellular carcinoma.
liver.overviewText: The liver is the largest internal organ. Most primary liver cancers develop in people with chronic liver disease, such as cirrhosis caused by Hepatitis B, C, or excessive alcohol use.

symptoms.symptom1: Unintended weight loss and loss of appetite.
symptoms.symptom2: Pain in the upper right abdomen.
symptoms.symptom4: Abdominal swelling (ascites) or visible veins on the belly.
symptoms.symptom5: White or chalky stools and dark urine.

liver.treatmentsIntro: Treatment is complex and relies heavily on the health of the remaining liver.

treatment1.title: Surgical Resection or Transplant
treatment1.desc: Tumor removal (if liver works well) or liver replacement.

treatment2.title: Ablation & Embolization Therapy
treatment2.desc: Techniques to destroy tumors directly without major surgery.

pancreatic.title: Pancreatic Cancer
pancreatic.shortDescription: Aggressive cancer starting in pancreatic tissues. Difficult to detect early.
pancreatic.overviewText: The pancreas aids digestion and regulates blood sugar. This cancer is often found late because it causes no early symptoms and is hidden behind other organs. It is one of the toughest cancers to treat.

symptoms.symptom1: Abdominal pain that radiates to the back.
symptoms.symptom2: Loss of appetite and unintended weight loss.

pancreatic.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is the only potential curative option but is possible in only a minority of cases.

treatment1.title: Whipple Procedure (Surgery)
treatment1.desc: Complex operation to remove the head of the pancreas and nearby organs.

treatment2.title: Chemotherapy (e.g., FOLFIRINOX)
treatment2.desc: Potent regimens to shrink tumors or control advanced disease.

stat1.label: Diagnosed at a localized stage in the US (2016–2022)

pancreatic.appointmentText: Find centers with high pancreatic volume.

thyroid.title: Thyroid Cancer
thyroid.shortDescription: Cancer in the thyroid gland, located at the base of the neck. Generally very treatable.
thyroid.overviewText: The thyroid makes hormones regulating metabolism. Most thyroid cancers (like papillary) grow slowly and have an excellent prognosis if treated properly.

symptoms.symptom1: A lump or nodule that can be felt through the skin of the neck.
symptoms.symptom2: Changes in voice, including persistent hoarseness.
symptoms.symptom4: Pain in the neck and throat.
symptoms.symptom5: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck.
symptoms.symptom6: Persistent cough not related to a cold.

thyroid.treatmentsIntro: Standard approach involves surgery often followed by hormone therapy.

treatment1.title: Thyroidectomy
treatment1.desc: Total or partial removal of the thyroid gland.

treatment2.title: Radioactive Iodine Therapy
treatment2.desc: Using radioactive iodine post-surgery to destroy any remaining thyroid tissue.

esophageal.title: Esophageal Cancer
esophageal.shortDescription: Cancer in the tube connecting the throat to the stomach (esophagus).
esophageal.overviewText: Often linked to smoking, heavy alcohol use, and chronic acid reflux (Barrett's esophagus). Two main types: squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma.

symptoms.symptom1: Difficulty or pain swallowing (dysphagia), getting worse over time.
symptoms.symptom2: Unintended weight loss.

esophageal.treatmentsIntro: Often requires a combination of therapies for best results.

treatment1.title: Esophagectomy
treatment1.desc: Surgery to remove the affected part of the esophagus and reconnect the stomach.

treatment2.title: Chemoradiotherapy
treatment2.desc: Combined use of chemo and radiation, often before surgery.

stomach.title: Stomach (Gastric) Cancer
stomach.shortDescription: Cancer forming in the stomach lining. Tends to develop slowly.
stomach.overviewText: Can develop over many years. H. pylori infection is a major cause, along with dietary factors. Early symptoms are often mistaken for minor stomach issues.

symptoms.symptom1: Indigestion, persistent severe heartburn.
symptoms.symptom2: Feeling bloated or full after eating small amounts.
symptoms.symptom3: Persistent nausea and vomiting (sometimes with blood).
symptoms.symptom6: Fatigue and weakness due to anemia.

stomach.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is the main curative option, often combined with other therapies.

treatment1.title: Gastrectomy (Total or Subtotal)
treatment1.desc: Removal of all or part of the stomach and nearby lymph nodes.

treatment2.title: Perioperative Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Given before and/or after surgery to improve outcomes.

multiple-myeloma.title: Multiple Myeloma
multiple-myeloma.shortDescription: Cancer of plasma cells, a type of white blood cell in bone marrow.
multiple-myeloma.overviewText: Cancer cells accumulate in bone marrow, crowding out healthy blood cells. They produce abnormal proteins that can cause kidney problems and damage bones.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent bone pain, especially in back, ribs, or hips.
symptoms.symptom2: Weak bones that fracture easily.
symptoms.symptom3: Extreme fatigue and weakness due to anemia.
symptoms.symptom5: Excessive thirst, confusion (due to high blood calcium).

multiple-myeloma.treatmentsIntro: Although generally not curable, it is treatable for many years with modern therapies.

treatment1.title: Targeted Therapy & Immunomodulators
treatment1.desc: Drugs like proteasome inhibitors that specifically attack myeloma cells.

treatment2.title: Autologous Stem Cell Transplant
treatment2.desc: Using patient's own stem cells to rescue marrow after high-dose chemo.

ovarian.title: Ovarian Cancer
ovarian.shortDescription: Cancer starting in ovaries or fallopian tubes. Often detected late.
ovarian.overviewText: Often has no symptoms until it has spread within the pelvis and abdomen. It is the leading cause of death from gynecologic cancers in the Western world.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent abdominal bloating or distention.
symptoms.symptom2: Feeling full quickly when eating or trouble eating.
symptoms.symptom3: Discomfort or pain in the pelvic or abdominal area.
symptoms.symptom4: Need to urinate more frequently or urgently.
symptoms.symptom5: Changes in bowel habits, such as constipation.

ovarian.treatmentsIntro: Usually involves a combination of aggressive surgery and chemotherapy.

treatment1.title: Debulking Surgery
treatment1.desc: Removal of as much visible tumor as possible from the abdomen.

treatment2.title: Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: The standard of care after surgery for most patients.

cervical.title: Cervical Cancer
cervical.shortDescription: Cancer in the lower part of the uterus. Highly preventable with vaccination and screening.
cervical.overviewText: Almost all cases are caused by persistent infection with high-risk types of Human Papillomavirus (HPV). Pap smears and HPV testing are crucial tools for early detection of precancers.

symptoms.symptom1: Vaginal bleeding after sexual intercourse.
symptoms.symptom2: Unusual vaginal discharge, which may be watery, thick, or foul-smelling.
symptoms.symptom3: Pelvic pain or pain during intercourse.
symptoms.symptom6: Fatigue, weight loss, or back pain in advanced stages.

cervical.treatmentsIntro: Treatment is very effective when cancer is detected in early stages.

treatment1.title: Surgery (Conization or Hysterectomy)
treatment1.desc: From removing cervical tissue to removing the uterus.

treatment2.title: Concurrent Chemoradiation
treatment2.desc: Simultaneous use of chemo and radiation for more advanced stages.

brain.title: Brain Tumor
brain.shortDescription: Growth of abnormal cells in the brain. Can be benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous).
brain.overviewText: There are 120+ types of brain and central nervous system tumors. Symptoms depend heavily on where the tumor is and what part of the brain it is affecting.

symptoms.symptom1: New headaches or change in headache pattern.
symptoms.symptom2: Unexplained nausea or vomiting, especially in the morning.
symptoms.symptom3: Vision problems (blurred, double vision, or peripheral loss).
symptoms.symptom4: Gradual loss of sensation or movement in an arm or leg.
symptoms.symptom5: Difficulty with balance, speech, or confusion.
symptoms.symptom6: Seizures in someone with no history of them.

brain.treatmentsIntro: Treatment requires a multidisciplinary team of neurosurgeons and oncologists.

treatment1.title: Neurosurgery (Craniotomy)
treatment1.desc: Main treatment to remove as much tumor as safely possible.

treatment2.title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery (e.g., Gamma Knife)
treatment2.desc: Using highly focused radiation to treat tumors without incision.

testicular.title: Testicular Cancer
testicular.shortDescription: Cancer developing in the testicles. More common in young men and highly treatable.
testicular.overviewText: Though rare overall, it is the most common cancer in men aged 15-35. The vast majority are germ cell tumors. Regular self-exam is key to early detection.

symptoms.symptom1: A painless lump or swelling on either testicle.
symptoms.symptom2: Feeling of heaviness in the scrotum.
symptoms.symptom3: Dull ache or discomfort in the lower abdomen or groin.
symptoms.symptom4: Sudden build-up of fluid in the scrotum.
symptoms.symptom5: Pain or discomfort in a testicle or the scrotum.
symptoms.symptom6: Enlargement or tenderness of the breasts (rare, due to hormones).

testicular.treatmentsIntro: Even when spread, testicular cancer is one of the most curable types of cancer.

treatment1.title: Radical Inguinal Orchiectomy
treatment1.desc: Surgery to remove the affected testicle through a groin incision.

treatment2.title: Cisplatin-Based Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Highly effective for disease that has spread beyond the testicle.

childhood.title: Childhood Cancer
childhood.shortDescription: Bringing hope and support to our little warriors and their families.
childhood.overviewText: Childhood cancer includes various types of tumors occurring in children and adolescents. While rare, medical advances have led to high survival rates. Common types include leukemia, brain tumors, and lymphomas.

symptoms.symptom1: Constant fatigue
symptoms.symptom2: Easy bruising

childhood.treatmentsIntro: Treatment is adapted to age and cancer type:

treatment1.title: Chemotherapy
treatment1.desc: Medications to destroy cancer cells.

treatment2.title: Radiation Therapy
treatment2.desc: High-energy rays to eliminate tumors.

childhood.appointmentText: You are not alone. Contact us for guidance.

myeloma.title: Multiple Myeloma
myeloma.shortDescription: Cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow.
myeloma.overviewText: Multiple myeloma affects plasma cells, a type of white blood cell that helps fight infections. These cancer cells accumulate in the bone marrow and can damage bones and affect healthy blood cell production.

symptoms.symptom1: Bone pain
symptoms.symptom2: Extreme fatigue

treatment1.title: Targeted Therapy
treatment1.desc: Drugs attacking specific proteins.

treatment2.title: Bone Marrow Transplant
treatment2.desc: Replacing diseased cells with healthy ones.

sarcoma.title: Sarcoma
sarcoma.shortDescription: Tumors in bones and soft tissues.
sarcoma.overviewText: Sarcomas are a diverse group of cancers originating in bones or soft tissues (muscles, fat, blood vessels). There are over 70 different subtypes, and treatment depends on the exact location.

symptoms.symptom1: Painless lump
symptoms.symptom2: Bone pain

treatment1.title: Surgery
treatment1.desc: Tumor removal with safe margins.

treatment2.title: Radiation
treatment2.desc: To shrink tumor before surgery.

sarcoma.appointmentText: We are here to help through the process.

bile-duct.title: Bile Duct Cancer
bile-duct.overviewText: This rare cancer forms in the bile ducts, the thin tubes carrying digestive bile. It is often detected when causing jaundice (yellow skin) or abdominal pain.

symptoms.symptom1: Jaundice (yellowing)
symptoms.symptom2: Intense itching

treatment1.title: Surgery
treatment1.desc: Removal of affected ducts.

treatment2.title: Biliary Stent
treatment2.desc: To unblock bile flow.

eye.title: Eye Cancer
eye.overviewText: Cancer in the eye can affect the outer parts (eyelids) or inner parts (uveal melanoma, retinoblastoma in kids). Eye exams are key for early detection.

symptoms.symptom1: Blurred vision
symptoms.symptom2: Dark spots

treatment1.title: Brachytherapy
treatment1.desc: Temporary radioactive plaque.

treatment2.title: Laser
treatment2.desc: To destroy small tumors.

oral.title: Oral Cancer
oral.shortDescription: Affects lips, tongue, and mouth cavity.
oral.overviewText: Oral cancer develops in the tissues of the mouth or throat. Tobacco and alcohol are major risk factors, as well as HPV in some cases.

symptoms.symptom1: Sores that won't heal
symptoms.symptom2: White/red patches

treatment1.title: Surgery
treatment1.desc: Tumor removal.

treatment2.title: Radiation
treatment2.desc: Post-op or main therapy.

throat.title: Throat Cancer
throat.overviewText: This cancer affects the pharynx (throat tube) or larynx (voice box). It can impact speech and swallowing, making rehabilitation a key part of treatment.

symptoms.symptom1: Voice changes
symptoms.symptom2: Persistent hoarseness

treatment1.title: Radiation
treatment1.desc: To preserve voice.

treatment2.title: Speech Therapy
treatment2.desc: Post-treatment rehab.

thymus.title: Thymoma
thymus.shortDescription: Cancer of the thymus gland in the chest.
thymus.overviewText: The thymus is a small organ in the chest producing white blood cells. Tumors here (thymomas) are rare and often linked to autoimmune diseases like myasthenia gravis.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent cough
symptoms.symptom2: Chest pain

treatment1.title: Thymectomy
treatment1.desc: Surgery to remove thymus.

treatment2.title: Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: If surgery isn't an option.

gallbladder.title: Gallbladder Cancer
gallbladder.shortDescription: Uncommon cancer developing in the gallbladder. Often detected late.
gallbladder.overviewText: The gallbladder is a small organ under the liver. This cancer is hard to diagnose because it often causes no specific signs early on. Sometimes found unexpectedly during surgery for gallstones.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent abdominal pain, especially upper right.
symptoms.symptom2: Nausea and vomiting.

gallbladder.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is the best option if the cancer hasn't spread.

treatment1.title: Extended Cholecystectomy
treatment1.desc: Removing gallbladder, part of liver, and nearby lymph nodes.

treatment2.title: Palliative Treatment
treatment2.desc: Procedures like stenting to relieve jaundice and pain.

vaginal.title: Vaginal & Vulvar Cancer
vaginal.shortDescription: Rare gynecologic cancers affecting external genitals and birth canal.
vaginal.overviewText: Vulvar cancer affects the external female genital area, while vaginal cancer affects the internal canal. Both are rare and often linked to HPV infection or advancing age.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent itching or burning on the vulva that doesn't improve.
symptoms.symptom2: Pain or tenderness in the genital area.
symptoms.symptom4: Skin changes on vulva like color or thickness.
symptoms.symptom5: A lump, mass, or open sore on the vulva.
symptoms.symptom6: Pain when urinating or during sex.

vaginal.treatmentsIntro: Treatment depends on location and stage, focusing on preserving function when possible.

treatment1.title: Surgery (Excision or Vulvectomy)
treatment1.desc: Removal of cancerous tissue and a margin of healthy tissue.

treatment2.title: Radiation & Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Often used together for more advanced tumors.

meningioma.title: Meningioma
meningioma.shortDescription: Tumor arising from meninges, the membranes surrounding brain and spinal cord.
meningioma.overviewText: It is the most common type of primary brain tumor. Most are benign (non-cancerous) and slow-growing, but they can cause problems by pressing on the brain or nerves. Some can be malignant.

symptoms.symptom1: Headaches that worsen over time.
symptoms.symptom2: Vision changes, like double or blurriness.
symptoms.symptom5: Gradual weakness in an arm or leg.
symptoms.symptom6: Hearing problems or ringing in the ears.

meningioma.treatmentsIntro: Treatment depends on size, location, symptoms, and patient age.

treatment1.title: Active Observation
treatment1.desc: Regular monitoring with scans for small, asymptomatic tumors.

treatment2.title: Surgery & Radiation
treatment2.desc: Surgical removal if causing symptoms, or radiation if surgery is risky.

ewing-sarcoma.title: Ewing Sarcoma
ewing-sarcoma.shortDescription: Rare cancer forming in bones or soft tissue around bones.
ewing-sarcoma.overviewText: Mainly affects children and young adults, appearing most often in long bones of legs, arms, pelvis, or chest. It is an aggressive cancer requiring intensive treatment.

symptoms.symptom1: Pain and swelling in the affected area (bone or joint).
symptoms.symptom2: A visible or palpable lump, which may feel warm.
symptoms.symptom4: Bone fractures occurring without major injury.
symptoms.symptom6: Pain worsening at night or with activity.

ewing-sarcoma.treatmentsIntro: Almost always involves combination of chemo, surgery, and/or radiation.

treatment1.title: Intensive Chemotherapy
treatment1.desc: Usually the first step to shrink tumor and treat metastasis.

treatment2.title: Limb-Salvage Surgery
treatment2.desc: Removing tumor while preserving the arm or leg whenever possible.

penile.title: Penile Cancer
penile.shortDescription: Rare cancer forming in the skin or tissues of the penis.
penile.overviewText: Uncommon in developed nations. Risk factors include HPV infection, not being circumcised, phimosis, smoking, and poor hygiene. Most are squamous cell carcinomas.

symptoms.symptom1: A lump, ulcer, or sore on the penis that doesn't heal.
symptoms.symptom2: Changes in penis skin color or thickness.
symptoms.symptom3: Reddish or velvety rash under foreskin.
symptoms.symptom4: Persistent or smelly discharge under foreskin.
symptoms.symptom5: Bleeding from penis or under foreskin.

penile.treatmentsIntro: Goal is eliminating cancer while preserving as much function and appearance as possible.

treatment1.title: Surgery (e.g., Mohs Surgery)
treatment1.desc: Precise removal of tumor layer by layer to save healthy tissue.

treatment2.title: Radiation & Topical Therapy
treatment2.desc: For very early stage cancers or as adjunct to surgery.

anal.title: Anal Cancer
anal.shortDescription: Cancer forming in the anal canal. Distinct from colorectal cancer.
anal.overviewText: Forms in the opening at end of digestive tract. Vast majority of cases are strongly associated with Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Often curable, especially when caught early.

symptoms.symptom1: Bleeding from anus or rectum (often first sign).
symptoms.symptom2: Pain or pressure in anal area.
symptoms.symptom4: A lump or mass near the anus.
symptoms.symptom5: Changes in bowel habits or stool diameter.

anal.treatmentsIntro: Main treatment is usually a combination of radiation and chemotherapy, which often avoids need for major surgery.

treatment1.title: Concurrent Chemoradiation
treatment1.desc: The 'gold standard', often curing cancer without operation.

treatment2.title: Salvage Surgery
treatment2.desc: Used if cancer doesn't respond to chemoradiation or recurs.

neuroblastoma.title: Neuroblastoma
neuroblastoma.shortDescription: Cancer forming in immature nerve tissue. Most common cancer in babies.
neuroblastoma.overviewText: Affects mostly children under 5. Often starts in adrenal glands (above kidneys) but can form in nerve tissue along spine, neck, chest, or abdomen.

symptoms.symptom1: A mass or lump in abdomen, neck, or chest.
symptoms.symptom2: Bulging eyes or dark circles around eyes ('raccoon eyes').
symptoms.symptom6: Trouble breathing or swallowing (if in chest/neck).

neuroblastoma.treatmentsIntro: Treatment is based on risk group (low, intermediate, high).

treatment1.title: Observation or Moderate Surgery
treatment1.desc: For low-risk tumors, sometimes only watching or simple surgery is needed.

treatment2.title: Intensive Multimodal Therapy
treatment2.desc: For high risk: high-dose chemo, surgery, radiation, and immunotherapy (e.g., dinutuximab).

neuroblastoma.appointmentText: Support for understanding diagnosis and risk.

retinoblastoma.title: Retinoblastoma
retinoblastoma.shortDescription: Rare eye cancer starting in the retina, light-sensitive tissue at back of eye.
retinoblastoma.overviewText: Affects mostly young children, usually before age 5. Can be hereditary (affecting both eyes) or non-hereditary (one eye). Early diagnosis is vital to save vision and life.

symptoms.symptom1: White reflection in pupil ('cat's eye') when photo taken with flash.
symptoms.symptom2: Strabismus ('lazy eye'), where one eye looks in or out.
symptoms.symptom3: Persistent redness or swelling of the eye.
symptoms.symptom5: Poor vision or blindness in affected eye.
symptoms.symptom6: Pupil of affected eye appears larger than the other.

retinoblastoma.treatmentsIntro: Goal is eliminating cancer and, if possible, preserving vision.

treatment1.title: Focal Therapies (Laser, Cryotherapy)
treatment1.desc: Applied directly to eye to destroy small tumors.

treatment2.title: Chemotherapy (Systemic or Intra-arterial)
treatment2.desc: To shrink tumor, sometimes injected directly into eye artery.

stat1.label: High cure rate in developed nations

retinoblastoma.appointmentText: Check any change in your child's eyes.

head-neck.title: Head & Neck Cancer
head-neck.shortDescription: Group of cancers starting in mouth, nose, throat, larynx, or salivary glands.
head-neck.overviewText: Most are squamous cell carcinomas starting in moist surfaces of head and neck. Tobacco and alcohol use are main risk factors, along with HPV infection (especially in oropharynx).

symptoms.symptom1: A sore in mouth that doesn't heal or red/white patch on gums or tongue.
symptoms.symptom2: Persistent sore throat or feeling of something stuck.
symptoms.symptom4: Difficulty or pain swallowing or chewing.
symptoms.symptom5: A painless lump or mass in the neck.
symptoms.symptom6: Persistent ear pain or unusual nasal congestion.

head-neck.treatmentsIntro: Treatment seeks to eliminate cancer while preserving critical functions like speaking and swallowing.

treatment1.title: Surgery
treatment1.desc: Removal of tumor and sometimes neck lymph nodes.

treatment2.title: Radiotherapy & Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Often used combined as main treatment or after surgery.

head-neck.appointmentText: Consult persistent mouth or throat changes.

leukemia.title: Leukemia
leukemia.shortDescription: Cancer of blood-forming tissues in body, including bone marrow and lymphatic system.
leukemia.overviewText: Leukemia causes production of large amounts of abnormal white blood cells that don't function properly, crowding out healthy blood cells (red cells, platelets). There are acute (fast-growing) and chronic (slow-growing) types.

symptoms.symptom1: Persistent fatigue, weakness, and pale skin (due to anemia).
symptoms.symptom2: Fever, chills, or frequent and severe infections.
symptoms.symptom4: Swollen lymph nodes (painless), enlarged liver or spleen.

leukemia.treatmentsIntro: Treatment depends on leukemia type (myeloid vs lymphoid, acute vs chronic) and age.

treatment1.title: Chemotherapy (Induction/Consolidation)
treatment1.desc: Main treatment, using potent drugs to kill leukemia cells.

treatment2.title: Bone Marrow/Stem Cell Transplant
treatment2.desc: Replacing diseased marrow with healthy cells from a donor.

nasopharynx.title: Nasopharyngeal Cancer
nasopharynx.shortDescription: Rare head and neck cancer starting in upper part of throat, behind nose.
nasopharynx.overviewText: Uncommon in most of world but frequent in parts of Asia and North Africa. Strongly associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Due to location, can be hard to detect early.

symptoms.symptom1: Painless lump in neck (often first sign).
symptoms.symptom2: Muffled hearing or hearing loss, usually in one ear.
symptoms.symptom6: Double vision or facial numbness (if affecting nerves).

nasopharynx.treatmentsIntro: Due to sensitive location, surgery is rarely the main treatment.

treatment1.title: Intensity-Modulated Radiotherapy (IMRT)
treatment1.desc: Main treatment, directing high radiation doses to tumor.

treatment2.title: Concurrent or Induction Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Used along with radiation to boost effectiveness in advanced stages.

nasopharynx.appointmentText: Consult persistent nasal or ear symptoms.

bone.title: Bone Cancer
bone.shortDescription: Cancer originating in bone (primary bone cancer). Includes osteosarcoma & chondrosarcoma.
bone.overviewText: Primary bone cancer is rare. Most common types are osteosarcoma (frequent in teens) and chondrosarcoma (in adults). Most cancers in bones are metastasis from other organs, not primary bone cancer.

symptoms.symptom1: Pain in the affected bone, which may worsen at night.
symptoms.symptom2: Swelling and tenderness near the pain area.
symptoms.symptom3: Bone fractures occurring with minor injury.
symptoms.symptom6: Difficulty moving or limping (if affecting leg).

bone.treatmentsIntro: Treatment depends on type of bone sarcoma, location, and stage.

treatment1.title: Limb-Salvage Surgery
treatment1.desc: Removing tumor and reconstructing bone with grafts or prosthetics, avoiding amputation.

treatment2.title: Neoadjuvant & Adjuvant Chemotherapy
treatment2.desc: Often used before surgery (to shrink tumor) and after (to kill remaining cells).

mesothelioma.title: Mesothelioma
mesothelioma.shortDescription: Aggressive cancer affecting lining of lungs (pleura), abdomen, or heart.
mesothelioma.overviewText: Rare but aggressive cancer caused almost exclusively by asbestos exposure. Symptoms can take decades (20-50 years) to appear after exposure. Pleural mesothelioma (lung lining) is most common.

symptoms.symptom1: Pain in the chest or under the rib cage.
symptoms.symptom2: Shortness of breath (dyspnea) due to fluid buildup.
symptoms.symptom4: Unusual lumps of tissue under skin on chest.

mesothelioma.treatmentsIntro: Often diagnosed in advanced stages, making treatment a challenge.

treatment1.title: Surgery (e.g., Pleurectomy)
treatment1.desc: In early stages, to remove affected lining and try to reduce tumor.

treatment2.title: Chemotherapy & Immunotherapy
treatment2.desc: Standard treatments to slow disease and improve quality of life.

mesothelioma.appointmentText: Find centers with experience in this disease.

small-intestine.title: Small Intestine Cancer
small-intestine.shortDescription: Uncommon cancer forming in small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, or ileum).
small-intestine.overviewText: Much less frequent than colon cancer. Types include adenocarcinoma, carcinoid tumors, lymphoma, and sarcoma. Due to vague symptoms, often diagnosed in later stages.

symptoms.symptom1: Abdominal pain or cramping, often in center of abdomen.
symptoms.symptom2: Nausea and vomiting.
symptoms.symptom4: Blood in stool (can make it black and tarry).
symptoms.symptom5: Anemia (low red blood cell count) causing fatigue.
symptoms.symptom6: Yellowing of skin (jaundice) if tumor blocks bile duct.

small-intestine.treatmentsIntro: Main treatment is surgery, but depends on specific tumor type and location.

treatment1.title: Surgical Resection
treatment1.desc: Removal of segment of small intestine containing tumor.

treatment2.title: Chemotherapy or Targeted Therapies
treatment2.desc: Used for specific types like lymphomas or GISTs.

vulvar.title: Vulvar Cancer
vulvar.shortDescription: Rare cancer occurring on external female genital area (vulva).
vulvar.overviewText: Usually forms slowly over many years, often preceded by precancerous changes. More common in older women, but HPV-related cases are increasing in younger women.

symptoms.symptom1: Constant itching (pruritus) on vulva that doesn't go away.
symptoms.symptom2: Pain or tenderness in vulvar area.
symptoms.symptom4: Skin color or thickness changes (red or white patches).
symptoms.symptom5: A lump, bump, or open sore on vulva.

vulvar.treatmentsIntro: Surgery is most common treatment, often combined with radiation in advanced stages.

treatment1.title: Vulvectomy (Partial or Radical)
treatment1.desc: Removal of part or all of vulva, depending on cancer extent.

treatment2.title: Sentinel Node Biopsy
treatment2.desc: Procedure to check if cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes.

vulvar.appointmentText: Any persistent vulvar change needs checking.

larynx.title: Laryngeal Cancer
larynx.shortDescription: Cancer affecting larynx (voice box). A type of head and neck cancer.
larynx.overviewText: Larynx plays crucial role in breathing, speaking, and swallowing. Smoking and heavy alcohol use are main risk factors. Often detectable early due to voice changes.

symptoms.symptom1: Hoarseness or voice changes persisting >3 weeks.
symptoms.symptom2: Sore throat or persistent cough.
symptoms.symptom5: A lump or mass in the neck.

larynx.treatmentsIntro: Goal is curing cancer while trying to preserve voice and swallowing ability.

treatment1.title: Radiotherapy
treatment1.desc: Often main treatment for small tumors, to save voice.

treatment2.title: Surgery (Laryngectomy)
treatment2.desc: Partial or total removal of larynx, needed in advanced cases.

larynx.appointmentText: Consult if you have persistent hoarseness.

moodBoost.title: Warrior Mood Boost
moodBoost.subtitle: How are you feeling today?
moodBoost.intro: Pick how you’re feeling today. Click a mood below to reveal your support message, a gentle tip, and words from a fellow cancer warrior — all taken from the book “One Mission: Thrive”.
moodBoost.bookFooter: All warrior quotes are from our book “One Mission: Thrive” — written with and by cancer survivors for cancer warriors like you.

anxious.label: Feeling Anxious?
anxious.support: Feeling anxious is valid. Let’s pause together and breathe. You’ve already survived so much.
anxious.tip: Pause and breathe deeply. Inhale for 4, hold for 4, exhale for 6.
anxious.quote: “You are stronger than you think. Take it one day at a time.”

sad.label: Feeling Sad?
sad.support: Sadness is part of healing. Give yourself space to feel without guilt.
sad.tip: If you can, play a song that comforts you. Or sit with the feeling without judgment.
sad.quote: “It’s okay to be sad and angry with your diagnosis, just don’t stay in that place. It WILL get better.”

overwhelmed.label: Feeling Overwhelmed?
overwhelmed.support: Overwhelm happens. Focus on one small thing you can control right now.
overwhelmed.tip: Name three small things you can control right now.
overwhelmed.quote: “One day at a time. One foot in front of the other.”

tired.label: Feeling Tired?
tired.support: Rest isn’t giving up. It’s a crucial part of recovery.
tired.tip: Let your body pause. Even a 5-minute reset counts.
tired.quote: “Rest when you need. Fight when you can.”

angry.label: Feeling Angry?
angry.support: Your anger is real and justified. Let’s channel it safely today.
angry.tip: If possible, release safely: shake out your hands, write it down, or go for a short walk.
angry.quote: “The pain of today gives new meaning to the happiness of tomorrow.”

lonely.label: Feeling Lonely?
lonely.support: Loneliness can feel heavy, but you’re part of a warrior community that sees you.
lonely.tip: Reach out with one text, or revisit a favorite photo or memory.
lonely.quote: “Cancer is scary, but we are all in this fight together. No one fights alone.”

hopeful.label: Feeling Hopeful?
hopeful.support: Hope lives in small moments. Let’s nurture it together today.
hopeful.tip: Write down one thing you’re looking forward to.
hopeful.quote: “You can’t control what happens in life, but you can control how you handle it.”

scared.label: Feeling Scared?
scared.support: Fear shows how much you care about life. Let’s face it one breath at a time.
scared.tip: Sit with the fear, name it, and breathe through it. If you can, tell someone you trust how you feel.
scared.quote: “Be scared and do it anyway. Growth lives on the other side.”

numb.label: Feeling Numb?
numb.support: Feeling numb is a natural response. Your emotions will return when they’re ready.
numb.tip: Try to notice one physical sensation: the temperature of your hands, the feeling of your clothes.
numb.quote: “It’s okay to pause. But don’t quit.”

guilty.label: Feeling Guilty?
guilty.support: You don’t have to carry guilt. None of this is your fault.
guilty.tip: Write one sentence of self-kindness, even if it feels weird.
guilty.quote: “You are not broken or defective, you’ve just been rearranged for the better.”

grateful.label: Feeling Grateful?
grateful.support: Gratitude doesn’t erase the pain, but it can soften it for a moment.
grateful.tip: Think of one small thing or person you’re grateful for today.
grateful.quote: “This life can be delicate… but God is weaving a beautiful story that is your life.”

motivated.label: Feeling Motivated?
motivated.support: Let’s use this spark of motivation. One small action today is a big win.
motivated.tip: Choose one tiny task today that makes you feel in control.
motivated.quote: “Never forget how brave you are. The mind is powerful.”

privacy.title: Privacy and Data Protection Notice
privacy.content:
1. Who is responsible for your data?

The controller is Asociația Tutti Cancer Warriors (“TCW”), a Romanian nonprofit association, CIF 50156252, based in Bucharest, Romania. For privacy questions or to exercise your rights, email tcw@tutticancerwarriors.org.

2. Data we collect

  • Website and security data: IP address, device/browser information, requested pages, date/time and security logs processed by our hosting provider.
  • Contact and peer-support data: name, contact details, messages, preferences and information you choose to share for matching and support.
  • Dream-support applications: identity and contact details, age, country, wish, eligibility evidence, cancer-diagnosis or treatment information, agreement, payment details and proof that support was used as agreed.
  • Donations: donor and transaction information supplied by payment providers, banks or by you. For cryptocurrency verification, a transaction hash and public blockchain data may be checked.
  • Stories and publicity: text, name, photographs, video, audio and consent choices that you submit.

3. Why we use data and our legal bases

  • To answer requests and take steps you ask us to take, and to administer a program or agreement.
  • To manage donations, accounting, fraud prevention, audits and legal obligations.
  • For our legitimate interests in operating and securing the website, keeping appropriate records and improving charitable services, where those interests do not override your rights.
  • With consent where required. Health data is special-category data and is processed on the basis of your explicit consent, unless another Article 9 GDPR condition clearly applies. Public use of your story, name or image uses separate, optional consent.

You may withdraw consent at any time for future processing. Withdrawal does not affect processing already carried out lawfully. If information is required to assess or administer a request, we may be unable to proceed without it.

4. Google application forms

Our application buttons open Google Forms, a service operated by Google. Google may process technical and form data under its own terms and privacy notice. Review the notice shown with the form before submitting health information. Please do not send medical records through ordinary email unless TCW has asked you to use an approved secure method.

5. Who receives data?

Access is limited to authorised TCW personnel and, where needed, assigned peer-support participants. We may use providers for hosting (Netlify), forms and document collection (Google), database services (Supabase), donations and payments (including PayPal, Better Giving, banks and cryptocurrency infrastructure), communications, accounting, legal advice and security. We may also disclose information to public authorities when legally required. Providers may use data only for the agreed service or under their own controller obligations.

6. International transfers

Some providers or recipients may be outside Romania or the European Economic Area. Where GDPR transfer rules apply, we use an adequacy decision, approved contractual safeguards or another lawful transfer mechanism, as appropriate. Public blockchain information is globally accessible by design.

7. How long we keep data

We keep data only as long as needed for the relevant program, request, agreement, safety issue or legal claim. Grant and donation records are retained for the periods required by applicable accounting, tax, audit and limitation rules. Health-verification material is restricted and kept only for as long as needed for eligibility, administration, audit or legal obligations, then deleted or anonymised where possible. Public stories remain published within the consent given until removed or consent is withdrawn, subject to lawful archival or recordkeeping needs. Provider security logs follow the provider’s configured retention period.

8. Your rights

Depending on the circumstances, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, or object to processing based on legitimate interests. You may withdraw consent at any time and complain to the Romanian supervisory authority, ANSPDCP, or another competent authority where you live. To make a request, email tcw@tutticancerwarriors.org. We may need to verify your identity.

9. Security

We use proportionate technical and organisational measures, including access controls and secure service providers. No internet transmission or storage system is completely secure, so please share only the information requested and use the designated submission method.

10. Cookies, local storage and analytics

TCW currently does not run Google Analytics, advertising pixels or marketing trackers and does not set analytics or marketing cookies on this website. The site uses a functional NEXT_LOCALE cookie for up to one year to remember the language you select. Because this preference is necessary to provide the language choice you request, we do not ask you to consent to inactive analytics or marketing categories. Our hosting provider still processes ordinary request and security logs. When you follow a link to Google Forms, a payment provider, social network or another external service, that service may use its own cookies under its own notice. If TCW later adds non-essential analytics, advertising or embedded services, they will not be activated until the required information and consent controls are in place.

11. Children

Dream-support applicants must be at least 18. Our online services are not directed at children who cannot lawfully provide the required consent. If you believe a child’s data was submitted without proper authorisation, contact us so we can assess and take appropriate action.

12. Changes and contact

We may update this Notice when our services or legal obligations change. The effective date above identifies the current version.

Asociația Tutti Cancer Warriors
Bucharest, Romania · CIF 50156252
Email: tcw@tutticancerwarriors.org
Website: https://tutticancerwarriors.org

peerPolicy.content:
1. Purpose

TCW Connect is a private peer-support program for adults affected by cancer. It connects people living with cancer with survivor mentors who have relevant lived experience. It is not medical care, therapy, crisis support or an emergency service.

2. Eligibility and mentor approval

  • Warriors: Adults who are newly diagnosed, in treatment, after treatment, living with recurrence or metastatic cancer may apply.
  • Survivor mentors: Adults with relevant lived cancer experience may apply when they feel able to support another person safely.
  • TCW approval: Confirming an email does not approve a mentor. TCW verifies identity and survivor experience before a mentor can enter matching. TCW may decline, suspend or close a profile to protect participants.

3. How matching works

Applicants give explicit consent for health-data processing, automated matching, limited-profile sharing, program emails and meeting scheduling. The system compares cancer experience, treatment experience, language, topics, communication preferences and availability. Before acceptance, each person sees only a limited private profile. Contact details are shared only after both people separately accept and confirm the safety rules.

After mutual acceptance, TCW creates a private Google Calendar event and Google Meet using the shared availability. Do not forward invitations or meeting links.

4. Safety and conduct

  • Be respectful, keep information confidential and respect boundaries.
  • Do not give medical instructions, diagnose, pressure anyone to change treatment, request money, promote products or pursue romantic or sexual contact.
  • Do not record, transcribe, screenshot or share private conversations or profiles.
  • Use professional medical, mental-health or emergency services when those services are needed.

5. Report and block

A participant may use Report and block from the private TCW Connect page at any time. The system immediately stops the connection, suspends the reported profile for TCW review and cancels future Google Meet events linked to that profile. TCW records the incident privately and may keep the profile suspended, reinstate it or close it after review. If there is immediate danger, contact local emergency services first.

6. Privacy

Profiles, proposals, connections and safeguarding reports are stored privately and encrypted. There is no public survivor directory. Health details are not placed in calendar titles or routine TCW alerts. Participants should share only what is necessary and should never forward a private portal link.

7. Ending participation

Participants may pause matching, decline a proposal or end a connection from their private page. Ending or blocking a connection cancels its future scheduled meeting. TCW may restrict participation when the rules are breached or safety cannot be confirmed.

8. Contact and disclaimer

Questions or concerns may be sent to tcw@tutticancerwarriors.org. TCW Connect provides peer support only and does not replace professional counseling, diagnosis or medical treatment.

mensHealthWeek.title: 2026 Men’s Health Week Toolkit
mensHealthWeek.theme: Theme: Men's Health: Closing the Gap
mensHealthWeek.welcomeText: Men face significant health disparities. They live 6 years less than women on average and are 25% less likely to seek medical care. This toolkit helps raise awareness and action.
mensHealthWeek.fact1Text: Prostate cancer affects 1 in 8 men; testicular cancer is most common among ages 15–44.
mensHealthWeek.fact2Text: Men are 3x more likely to die by suicide; only 50% seek help when depressed.
mensHealthWeek.fact3Text: Leading cause of death; 50% of men have high blood pressure by age 55.
mensHealthWeek.quote1: “Men are 3x more likely to die by suicide.”
mensHealthWeek.quote2: “Prostate cancer is the 2nd leading cause of cancer death in men.”
mensHealthWeek.quote3: “Wear blue on Friday to show support!”

kidneyCancerDay.title: 2026 World Kidney Cancer Day Toolkit
kidneyCancerDay.theme: Theme: Show Your Kidneys Some Love
kidneyCancerDay.whyText: Kidney cancer is among the 10 most common cancers in both men and women. Yet many people don’t know the symptoms or risk factors. Early detection can save lives.
kidneyCancerDay.fact1: 1 in 10 people will have a kidney cyst or tumor at some point.
kidneyCancerDay.fact2: Hematuria (blood in urine) is a common early symptom, but often ignored.
kidneyCancerDay.fact3: High blood pressure and smoking are major risk factors.
kidneyCancerDay.fact4: Flank pain or a lump in the side or back may be a warning sign.
kidneyCancerDay.fact5: Obesity increases risk — maintaining a healthy weight is protective.
kidneyCancerDay.socialText: Use these sample captions and the hashtag #WorldKidneyCancerDay.
kidneyCancerDay.quote1: “Think kidney cancer is rare? It’s one of the top 10 most common cancers. Know the signs.”

aboutCancerPage.title: Learn about <highlight>Cancer</highlight>
aboutCancerPage.subtitle: Comprehensive information about cancer types, symptoms, early detection, and treatments. We're here to support you every step of the way.

breast.title: Breast Cancer
breast.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in breast tissue, most often in the ducts or lobules, and can affect people of any sex.

lung.title: Lung Cancer
lung.shortDesc: Cancer that forms in lung tissue, usually in cells lining the airways, with several types that require different treatment.

colorectal.title: Colorectal Cancer
colorectal.shortDesc: Cancer of the colon or rectum that often begins in a polyp and may cause bowel changes, bleeding or abdominal discomfort.

prostate.title: Prostate Cancer
prostate.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the prostate gland; some tumours grow slowly while others can spread more quickly.

skin.title: Skin Cancer
skin.shortDesc: This guide focuses on melanoma, a skin cancer that begins in pigment-producing cells and can spread if not treated early.

kidney.title: Kidney Cancer
kidney.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in kidney tissue, most commonly as renal cell carcinoma in adults.

leukemia.title: Leukemia
leukemia.shortDesc: A group of cancers of blood-forming tissues that cause abnormal blood cells to build up in blood and bone marrow.

liver.title: Liver Cancer
liver.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the liver, most often hepatocellular carcinoma, frequently in a liver already affected by chronic disease.

pancreatic.title: Pancreatic Cancer
pancreatic.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the pancreas; the most common type forms in cells that make digestive enzymes.

ovarian.title: Ovarian Cancer
ovarian.shortDesc: A group of cancers affecting the ovaries, with epithelial tumours the most common; symptoms can be persistent but nonspecific.

childhood.title: Childhood Cancer
childhood.shortDesc: A broad group of cancers diagnosed in children, including leukemias, brain tumours, lymphomas and solid tumours.

brain.title: Brain Tumor
brain.shortDesc: Tumours that begin in the brain or central nervous system; they may be benign or malignant but can still require specialist care.

bladder.title: Bladder Cancer
bladder.shortDesc: Cancer that usually begins in the urothelial cells lining the bladder and often first appears as blood in the urine.

cervical.title: Cervical Cancer
cervical.shortDesc: Cancer of the cervix that is usually linked to persistent high-risk HPV infection and can often be prevented through vaccination and screening.

stomach.title: Stomach Cancer
stomach.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the stomach, most often in gland-forming cells of its inner lining.

testicular.title: Testicular Cancer
testicular.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in a testicle, usually in germ cells, and most often affects younger and middle-aged men.

thyroid.title: Thyroid Cancer
thyroid.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the thyroid gland in the neck and includes several types with very different behaviour.

uterine.title: Uterine Cancer
uterine.shortDesc: Cancer of the uterine body, most commonly endometrial cancer, which often causes abnormal vaginal bleeding.

lymphoma.title: Lymphoma
lymphoma.shortDesc: A large group of cancers of the lymphatic system, including Hodgkin and many types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

myeloma.title: Multiple Myeloma
myeloma.shortDesc: Cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow that can affect bones, kidneys, blood counts and immunity.

esophageal.title: Esophageal Cancer
esophageal.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the oesophagus, the tube carrying food from the throat to the stomach.

head-neck.title: Head & Neck
head-neck.shortDesc: A group of cancers that can begin in the mouth, throat, voice box, nose, sinuses or salivary glands.

bone.title: Bone Cancer
bone.shortDesc: Rare cancers that begin in bone, including osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma.

sarcoma.title: Sarcoma
sarcoma.shortDesc: A diverse group of cancers that begin in soft tissues such as muscle, fat, nerves, blood vessels and connective tissue.

gallbladder.title: Gallbladder Cancer
gallbladder.shortDesc: A rare cancer that begins in the gallbladder and is often found after it has grown beyond this small organ.

bile-duct.title: Bile Duct Cancer
bile-duct.shortDesc: Also called cholangiocarcinoma, this cancer begins in bile ducts inside or outside the liver.

anal.title: Anal Cancer
anal.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the tissues of the anus, with most cases linked to persistent high-risk HPV infection.

penile.title: Penile Cancer
penile.shortDesc: A rare cancer that begins in penile tissue, most often in squamous cells of the skin.

vaginal.title: Vaginal Cancer
vaginal.shortDesc: A rare cancer that begins in the vagina, most commonly in squamous cells lining its surface.

vulvar.title: Vulvar Cancer
vulvar.shortDesc: Cancer that begins on the external female genital tissues and may appear as persistent itching, pain or skin changes.

eye.title: Eye Cancer
eye.shortDesc: A group of rare cancers affecting the eye, including uveal melanoma in adults and retinoblastoma in children.

oral.title: Oral Cancer
oral.shortDesc: Cancer that begins in the lips or oral cavity, including the tongue, gums, inner cheeks and floor or roof of the mouth.

throat.title: Throat Cancer
throat.shortDesc: An informal term for cancers that arise in parts of the pharynx or larynx, each with distinct risks and treatments.

small-intestine.title: Small Intestine
small-intestine.shortDesc: A rare group of cancers that begin in the small intestine, including adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumours, lymphoma and sarcoma.

thymus.title: Thymus Cancer
thymus.shortDesc: Rare tumours that begin in the thymus behind the breastbone, mainly thymoma and thymic carcinoma.

diagnosisPage.title: Understanding Your Diagnosis
diagnosisPage.heroDesc: Navigating a cancer diagnosis can be overwhelming. We are here to help you make sense of the medical terms, staging, and next steps.
diagnosisPage.whatIsCancerDesc: Cancer is a group of diseases involving abnormal cell growth with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body. Understanding the basics is the first step in taking control.
diagnosisPage.stagingDesc: Staging describes the extent of cancer in the body. It is usually based on the size of the tumor, whether lymph nodes contain cancer, and whether the cancer has spread from the original site.

stages.0: Abnormal cells present but have not spread.
stages.II: Cancer has grown but is still localized.
stages.III: Cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes.
stages.IV: Cancer has spread to other parts of the body.

diagnosisPage.gradingDesc: Grading describes how the cancer cells look compared to normal cells. It gives an idea of how quickly the cancer may grow and spread.
diagnosisPage.aloneDesc: Receiving a diagnosis is just the start of your journey as a warrior. Our community is here to support you, listen to you, and fight alongside you.

emotionalPage.title: Emotional Well-Being for Cancer Warriors
emotionalPage.desc: Caring for your emotional health is just as important as managing the physical side of cancer. This guide offers practical tools to help you stay mentally and emotionally strong throughout your journey.
emotionalPage.ctaDesc: Take these emotional well-being strategies with you. Print or save for easy reference during difficult times.

anxiety.title: Coping with Anxiety
tech1_steps: Find a quiet space, sit or lie down comfortably
Close your eyes and take a slow, deep breath in through your nose
Allow your abdomen to rise, hold for a few seconds
Repeat several times, focusing on the sensation of your breath
tech2_steps: Inhale through your nose for a count of 4
Hold the breath for a count of 7
Exhale through your mouth for a count of 8
This helps slow your breathing and can be effective before sleep
tech3_steps: When anxious thoughts creep in, identify and challenge them
Ask if thoughts are based on facts or assumptions
Replace negative thoughts with balanced, realistic ones
tech4_steps: Focus on the present moment rather than worrying about the future
Engage fully in activities: eating, walking, observing
Mindfulness reduces anxiety by anchoring you in the here and now

depression.title: Dealing with Depression
signs: Persistent Sadness: Feeling sad or hopeless for extended periods
Loss of Interest: Lack of interest in activities you once enjoyed
Fatigue: Feeling exhausted even after adequate rest
Changes in Appetite: Significant weight loss or gain
Difficulty Concentrating: Trouble focusing or making decisions
depression.help1_desc: Speaking with a mental health professional provides strategies to manage depression
depression.help2_desc: Connecting with others who have faced similar challenges can be incredibly comforting
depression.help3_desc: In some cases, medication may be necessary. Always consult with a healthcare professional

positivity.title: Maintaining Positivity
positivity.prac1_desc: Each day, write down three things you are grateful for. These can be small things like a warm cup of tea or a kind word from a friend
positivity.prac2_desc: Expressing gratitude to others can lift your spirits. Writing a thank you note fosters positive emotions
positivity.prac3_desc: Engage in activities that bring you joy: reading, listening to music, or spending time in nature
positivity.prac4_desc: Explore creative outlets like drawing, writing, or crafting to process emotions

support.title: Support Networks
pt1_items: Open Communication: Let loved ones know how they can support you
Quality Time: Spend time with those who make you feel good
Engaging in activities together provides comfort and normalcy
pt2_items: Shared Experiences: Connect with others who understand what you are going through
Safe Space: Share stories, ask for advice, and receive encouragement
Mentorship: Some programs match you with a survivor mentor

fullContent.missionText: Asociația Tutti Cancer Warriors (TCW) supports the emotional and practical well-being of adults affected by cancer. An applicant must be at least 18, provide acceptable verification of a cancer diagnosis, and be in a country where TCW can lawfully and operationally provide support. Each application is assessed individually by TCW; applying does not guarantee approval.
fullContent.scopeIntro: An approved grant supports a non-medical personal wish with a value of up to €500. TCW does not fund medical treatment or medication. The approved purpose, amount, method and conditions are recorded in the grant agreement.
fullContent.wishesText: A wish may include an appropriate experience, item or well-being activity. Subject to the agreement, TCW may buy the item or service directly, pay a supplier, reimburse approved documented costs, or transfer funds to the beneficiary. Support is normally fulfilled within 30 days after approval is complete, the required funds are available and all agreement conditions have been met.
fullContent.nonTransferableText: Support is only for the named beneficiary and approved wish. It may not be transferred, sold or used for a different purpose without TCW’s written approval.
fullContent.adminCostsText: The maximum value is €500, not a guaranteed fixed payment. The final value may be lower and depends on the approved wish, available funds, lawful payment options and the signed agreement.
fullContent.legalBasisText: TCW is a Romanian nonprofit association operating under Government Ordinance no. 26/2000, approved and amended by Law no. 246/2005, its Statute and other applicable law. Cross-border support remains subject to sanctions, payment and local legal restrictions.
fullContent.financeText: The beneficiary must provide the evidence specified in the agreement, such as receipts or supplier confirmation, within 3 months after the support is fulfilled or funds are received. TCW keeps financial and grant records for the periods required by applicable law.
fullContent.auditText: TCW reviews submitted proof within 15 calendar days after receiving it. If evidence is incomplete, TCW may request reasonable clarification or replacement documents and will record the outcome. Medical and supporting documents are kept confidential with access limited to authorised persons.
fullContent.gdprText: Personal data is processed under the Privacy Notice and GDPR. Health data requires an applicable Article 9 basis, normally explicit consent. Permission to publish a name, story, image or campaign is separate, optional and does not affect eligibility; anonymity is available.
fullContent.crossBorderText: TCW selects a lawful and practical fulfilment method. Beneficiaries are responsible for checking any personal tax or reporting duties in their country; TCW does not provide tax advice.
fullContent.disputesText: Concerns should first be raised with TCW so the parties can seek a fair, documented solution. Romanian law applies without removing mandatory rights under other applicable law. Any unresolved dispute is handled by the competent courts unless the grant agreement lawfully provides otherwise.
fullContent.terminationText: Fraud, material misrepresentation, transfer or misuse of support, or unjustified failure to provide agreed proof may lead to suspension, termination or a proportionate repayment request after notice and an opportunity to explain. TCW may waive or adjust a remedy where serious illness or hardship makes that fair and lawful.
fullContent.forceMajeureText: If serious illness, force majeure or another event outside the beneficiary’s reasonable control prevents timely fulfilment or proof, TCW may approve a written extension of up to 6 months. The beneficiary should contact TCW as soon as reasonably possible.
